draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kalpetta! It's the headquarters of Wayanad, the only plateau in Kerala, and it sits at about 780 m among coffee and tea plantations.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat in Kalpetta, so ask a local, you're in coffee country after all.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Kalpetta Juma Masjid is a 2 min walk. Banasura Dam is 15 km northwest, and Pookote Lake is near Vythiri.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Pookote Lake is a freshwater lake ringed by evergreen hills, with boating if you fancy it.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Banasura is considered the second largest earth dam in Asia. When the reservoir filled, it left a set of islands behind.

spots.name: Kalpetta Juma Masjid (Valiya Palli)
spots.detail: 2 min walk · The town's big mosque

spots.name: Banasura Dam
spots.detail: 15 km away · Earth dam with islands

spots.name: Pookote Lake
spots.detail: Near Vythiri · Freshwater lake with boating

legends.title: The Chain Tree
legends.body: A tribal youth showed an English engineer the route for the ghat road, and was killed for it. His angry spirit caused accidents until a priest chained it to a tree at Lakkidi.

legends.title: The mahout's spirit
legends.body: Another telling says Adivasi mahouts led the British up the mountains and were killed so they couldn't guide the Portuguese. Drivers still pray at the tree for a safe trip.

tips.title: Start treks at Banasura.
tips.body: The dam area is the starting point for treks up Banasura Peak.

tips.title: Go early to Lakkidi.
tips.body: The viewpoint can get busy and littered in peak season.

story.title: Hill people
story.body: Many indigenous tribes have lived on the Wayanad plateau.

story.title: A new district
story.body: Wayanad district was formed on 1 November 1980, carved out of Kozhikode and Kannur, with Kalpetta as its headquarters.

story.title: Where the Kabini begins
story.body: The Kabini River, a tributary of the Kaveri, starts in Wayanad.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Plantations, a dam and a lake all within reach. Tell me which way you headed.
